security_spec.violation_condition: In XiangShan RTL, if any G-stage-only PTW path (e.g., s2xlate === onlyStage2 or allStage G-stage walk) processes a G-stage PTE with the N bit set without treating it as an Svnapot 64KB page — specifically, failing to merge vpn[pteNapotBits-1:0] into the PPN lower bits — or if a PtwEntry/PtwSectorEntry instantiated for G-stage contexts omits hasNapot=true, or if the G-stage PTE tag comparison does not use the truncated tag match (pteNapotBits-based) when n=1, the hardware produces an incorrect guest physical address, violating the spec requirement that Svnapot is supported in G-stage translation.
security_spec.summary: G-stage (guest-stage) page table walker must recognize and correctly decode Svnapot N bit in hypervisor-managed page tables: PPN must merge vpn[3:0] into ppn[3:0] when N=1, tag matching must truncate to pteNapotBits boundary, and all G-stage PTE entry containers (HptwResp, PtwMergeResp) must carry hasNapot=true, or else guest physical addresses will be silently miscomputed, causing cross-VM data corruption.

findings.finding: HptwResp (G-stage PTW response) instantiates PtwEntry with hasNapot=true, ensuring the N bit is preserved for G-stage Svnapot 64KB page translation.
findings.snippet:
class HptwResp(implicit p: Parameters) extends PtwBundle {
  val entry = new PtwEntry(tagLen = gvpnLen, hasPerm = true, hasLevel = true, hasNapot = true)

findings.finding: HptwResp.apply() computes N field as (pte.n==1 && ppn[3:0]==8 && level==0), ensuring only valid Svnapot 64KB encodings set the napot bit. Invalid encodings (wrong PPN or non-0 level) are correctly zeroed.
genPPNS2() at level 0 merges vpn[pteNapotBits-1:0] into PPN low bits when N!=0, producing the correct guest physical address for Svnapot 64KB pages in G-stage translation.
G-stage TLB hit check uses truncated tag comparison (vpn[vpnnLen-1:pteNapotBits] vs tag[vpnnLen-1:pteNapotBits]) when n!=0, correctly matching any vpn within the 64KB Svnapot region.
findings.snippet:
tag_match(0) := Mux(entry.n.getOrElse(0.U) === 0.U,
  entry.tag(vpnnLen - 1, 0) === gvpn(vpnnLen - 1, 0),
  entry.tag(vpnnLen - 1, pteNapotBits) === gvpn(vpnnLen - 1, pteNapotBits))

findings.finding: allStage_n logic correctly composes napot across two-stage translation: napot is valid when (S1=napot && S2=superpage) || (S2=napot && S1=superpage) || (both napot). The smaller of the two translations determines 64KB page granularity, and getVpn() uses inner_n for vpn reconstruction at level 0.
last_hptw_req_ppn correctly merges vpn low 4 bits into PPN when N bit is set, producing the correct G-stage physical address for Svnapot pages during allStage PTW walks.
findings.snippet: val last_hptw_req_ppn = Mux(last_hptw_req_pte.n === 0.U, last_hptw_req_pte.getPPN(), Cat(last_hptw_req_pte.getPPN()(ptePPNLen - 1, pteNapotBits), io.in.bits.req_info.vpn(pteNapotBits - 1, 0)))

findings.finding: Memory response PPN generation in PTW entry applies the same napot-aware merge (vpn low bits into PPN), ensuring consistency across both last_hptw_req and normal PTW memory response paths.
findings.snippet: entries(i).ppn := Mux(ptes(index).n === 0.U, ptes(index).getPPN(), Cat(ptes(index).getPPN()(ptePPNLen - 1, pteNapotBits), entries(i).req_info.vpn(pteNapotBits - 1, 0)))

findings.finding: TlbSectorEntry (sector TLB storage) uses identical allStage_n logic to PtwRespS2 for self-tracking the napot bit when merging two-stage translation results into TLB entries.

PtwMergeEntry created with hasNapot=true for contiguous PTE merging; N field computed as (n==1 && ppn[3:0]==8); napot entries correctly suppress not_super flag, ensuring proper TLB entry classification for G-stage napot pages.
findings.snippet:
val ptw_resp = Wire(new PtwMergeEntry(tagLen = sectorvpnLen, hasPerm = true, hasLevel = true, hasNapot = true))
ptw_resp.n.map(_ := pte_in.n === true.B && pte_in.getPPN()(3, 0) === 8.U)
val napot = ptw_merge_resp.entry(vpn(sectortlbwidth - 1, 0)).n.getOrElse(0.U)
ptw_merge_resp.not_super := not_super.B && !napot

findings.finding: G-stage page fault detection (isGpf) correctly validates Svnapot: N!=0 with wrong ppn[3:0] encoding triggers gpf; non-leaf PTEs with N!=0 are caught by isNext() check; unaligned() catches napot at wrong levels for leaf PTEs.
TLB response path for onlyStage2 correctly uses genPPNS2(gvpn) to produce the G-stage physical address, which includes napot-aware VPN-to-PPN merging for 64KB pages.

findings.finding: G-stage-only PTW uses isGpf() for page fault detection, which includes the Svnapot encoding validation and will correctly fault on invalid N/PPN combinations.
